conviction_note: Near non-result. The bar ($0.95-0.96 consensus) sits on the company's own Q3 guide (NIM ~3.45%, opex $34.5-35M, fees ~$8M, tax 19.5%), which works out to roughly flat EPS against Q2's $0.96. The only new information since SMBK last spoke is peer evidence of Tennessee deposit-cost pressure (FBK NIM -12bp, FHN interest-bearing deposit costs +12bp), a small negative proxy. It is offset by SMBK's 15% annualised loan growth momentum, a 16 Sep Fed hike that helps the forward margin if SMBK is asset-sensitive (not verified), and a reaction history of 6 up in 7. findings.finding: Management guided Q3 2026 NIM to about 3.45%, down from 3.52% reported and 3.48% normalised ex-prepayment fees in Q2, citing deposit cost pressure. It also guided nonint. expense to $34.5-35M (Q2 $34.0M), nonint. income to ~$8M and tax to 19.5%. With about 3% QoQ earning-asset growth this works out to roughly $0.95 EPS, i.e. the $0.95-0.96 consensus sits on the guide. A modestly lower NIM is the expectation, not a surprise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: NIM +4bp and EPS $0.96 against the guide, stock +1.95% (baseline 2026-07-20). 6 of 7 recent prints rose, median absolute move 2.98%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. The guide is public and consensus sits on it. Filed so the judges see where the bar comes from. If the market expected a margin above the guide, consensus would be above $0.96 rather than at $0.95-0.96.
findings.independence: Q2 numbers are from the company 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001038773/000110465926085102/smbk-20260720xex99d1.htm. The guide numbers are from one secondary summary only.

findings.finding: Two Tennessee peers that reported after SMBK last spoke on 21 July show deposit-cost pressure in Q3 2026. FB Financial (Nashville, 13 Oct): NIM 3.83%, down 12bp QoQ, mainly on funding costs; cost of deposits 2.26% to 2.32%; CFO: 'We expect funding competition to remain elevated'; revenue missed by about $7M. First Horizon (Memphis, 15 Oct): interest-bearing deposit costs +12bp to 2.45%, NIM down 1bp to 3.48%. SMBK's Q2 cost of deposits rose only 3bp (2.12% to 2.15%) while loans grew 15% annualised and time deposits rose $116M in H1. A peer-sized funding squeeze would put SMBK's NIM at or below the 3.45% guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No SMBK print in the 7-quarter baseline missed on margin. The margin has expanded since 2025 (3.29% in Q2 2025 to 3.52%), and those prints rose. No history of how SMBK trades a margin miss.
findings.why_not_priced: The peer prints came after SMBK's last update, and SMBK consensus ($0.95-0.96, last dated 3 Aug on Tickflow) shows no visible revision for them. If the market had marked SMBK's margin down on the peer read, the stock would have lagged into the print. Instead it is 5% from its high with a -2% 20d run-up, which is flat for a bank. The guide already embeds some deposit pressure, so this is a partial, proxy-level item.
findings.independence: First Horizon release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036966/000003696626000178/a3q2026earningsrelease.htm. FBK primary release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649749/000164974926000063/a3q26pressreleasetablesfor.htm. Counter-evidence: Home BancShares (14-15 Oct) cited 'disciplined funding costs' and margin expansion (https://finviz.com/news/402737/home-bancshares-reports-record-third-quarter-net-income-bringing-the-company-closer-to-a-half-billion-dollar-year). This is a proxy; SMBK has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: On 16 Sep 2026 the Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, its first hike since 2023, and most officials projected at least one more hike in 2026. This hike landed after SMBK gave its Q3 guide and only affects the last two weeks of Q3. Its main bearing is on the Q4 margin commentary on the 20 Oct call. FBK said each 25bp hike adds about 3bp to its margin. SMBK's rate sensitivity was not verified (the 10-Q market-risk section could not be read), but loan repricing drove its Q2 margin expansion.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No SMBK history of a rate-hike margin outlook. The company gives qualitative and near-term margin guidance on the call, and the Q2 'modest margin expansion over time' comment came with a +1.95% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The macro event is fully public. What the market lacks is SMBK's own translation of it into a Q4 margin view. If an asset-sensitive tailwind were priced, the stock would have re-rated after 16 Sep, but it is -2% over 20 days. This is macro-to-company transmission and its sign depends on SMBK's unverified asset/liability sensitivity.
findings.independence: FBK sensitivity comment in the same call summary as finding 2 (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-2160603-20261014); that document is shared with finding 2. FHN expects its margin to rise into the 3.50% range (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262219385-tradingkey).

findings.finding: SMBK grew loans $165M in Q2 2026 (about 15% annualised) and core deposits about 6% annualised. The CEO said pipelines 'remain healthy' and that competitor disruption is creating 'meaningful opportunities', likely meaning the Pinnacle-Synovus integration that closed 1 Jan 2026. Guided salary costs of $21-21.5M reflect new hires. Another quarter of double-digit loan growth would lift net interest income enough to offset the guided margin decline, and growth ahead of the ~3% QoQ implied in consensus is the main route to a beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: 15% annualised loan growth with EPS $0.96 (from $0.81), stock +1.95%. Q1 2025 and Q4 2024 rose 6.7% and 8.1% on growth-led beats (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: price targets were raised after Q2 and the stock trades near its high. The unpriced piece is whether growth continued at Q2's pace while peers lost loan-pricing discipline (FBK cites competitors doing owner-occupied CRE 'in the 5s'). Consensus flat on Q2 at $0.95-0.96 suggests the street is not extrapolating 15% growth.
findings.independence: FBK loans grew 9.7% annualised in Q3 and the Nashville market had a 'really, really strong deposit quarter' (https://briefglance.com/articles/fb-financial-surges-in-q3-organic-growth-masks-margin-squeeze), which supports regional demand. The quarter's company documents are shared with finding 1.

findings.finding: Short interest nearly doubled into the print: 333,431 shares (1.95% of shares out) on 2026-07-31 to 636,039 (3.72%, 3.94 days to cover) on 2026-09-30. Bearish positioning is building on a thin name trading about 110k shares a day. It is not crowded enough for a squeeze mechanism, but it is a directional statement by someone. The cause is unidentified: no M&A arbitrage or index event was found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Earlier settlements (Apr 2026 DTC 3.08, Jun 1.97) preceded the +0.9% (Q1) and +1.95% (Q2) prints, so there is no visible relation.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public with a lag, and the position has already been put on, so any information it reflects is partly in the price. If the shorts are informed about the margin (finding 2), a miss would hit harder. If they are hedges, a beat on a 4-day-to-cover thin float squeezes. The sign is genuinely ambiguous, which is why the size is small.

findings.finding: The EVP and Chief Credit Officer sold small lots on the open market: 430 shares at $52.75 on 2026-08-04 and 230 at $52.05 on 2026-09-14, leaving 11,142 shares. No insider purchases were found for Aug-Oct 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: The amounts are immaterial (under $35k combined). A credit officer selling would matter if credit were turning; the Q2 data (nonperforming assets 0.23% of assets, net charge-offs $553K) shows no sign of that.
